newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares seen poised for further rises.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares seen poised for further rises.

text.p: Shanghai's foreign currency B shares, up nearly 30 percent since the beginning of the year, are poised for further rises in 1997 on rosy fundamentals, analysts said on Thursday.

Several traders said the B share index could breach the historical high of 105.78 points, set in December 1993, in July or August this year with 1997 interim company results expected to improve sentiment further.
The index closed on Thursday at 86.257, up 0.610 points, or 0.71 percent.
A research paper by Shenyin & Wanguo Securities, China's top brokerage, agreed on a continued upward trend for 1997 but gave no prediction of how far it would go.
"There are reasons to believe that 1997 will be the best year for B share market development since its establishment in 1992," the research paper said.
"The Shanghai B share market performed well in the first quarter of 1997. We expect a continuous upward trend on this market during the rest of 1997," it added.
"The index has been rising steadily in the past few months and the trend is expected to continue for the rest of this year," said a B share investment analyst with a major Chinese securities house.
"It is likely to breach the record high in July or August with listed firms expected to post much better interim results for 1997 than 1996," she added.
Analysts agreed official statistics indicated China's economy was continuing to improve in the first quarter of this year after last year's good performance.
Retail price inflation fell to a year-on-year 2.6 percent in the first three months of the year against a year-on-year 6.1 percent for the whole of 1996 and 14.8 percent in 1995.
"The improvement in the national economy is the main factor driving the B share market," said the Shenyin & Wanguo research paper.
Helping the positive mood was strong 1996 results from many blue-chip Shanghai firms, their share prices hitting record highs in the past few weeks, analysts said.
These included portable phone maker Eastern Communications Co, Dazhong Taxi Co, Shanghai Refrigerator Compressor Co and textile firm Shanghai Worldbest Co, they said.
The full impact of the improved economy on company performance was expected to be seen in the 1997 results, analysts said.
The Shenyin research paper said standardisation of the B share market was another favourable factor.
"Since the end of 1996, the authorities have published a series of regulations and measures to guide the market towards healthy development," the paper said.
"Those regulations and measures will eventually have an impact on the B share market in 1997."
"They will help stabilise investors currently in the market and attract many more in the near future. This favourable situation will surely push the market a further step."
